analyst_view.overall: Early view: Trabzonspor (2nd, three points behind) have won all six league games under Thomas Reis, the latest 2-0 at Alanyaspor, though they lost 1-0 at home to Freiburg in the Conference League. Eyupspor are bottom with three points and a 3-30 goal difference, and coach Mustafa Dalci admitted after the 2-0 home loss to Kocaelispor that things are not going well. Trabzonspor's long-term absentees include Ruslan Malinovskyi and Batagov.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and I lean slightly higher. Eyupspor have conceded 30 goals in eleven games, including five at Amed, and Trabzonspor have scored 26 while conceding only eight, so the risk is a heavy home win rather than a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Trabzonspor gave Alanyaspor almost no possession last week and should do the same here, so nearly all corners should be theirs; Eyupspor's 3.6 looks high, but Trabzonspor's own share could be bigger, so the total holds.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards and I lean lower. One-sided games like this rarely produce many bookings, and Trabzonspor have little need to foul when they control the ball the way they did in Alanya.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots. I expect Trabzonspor to take well over their 17.2 and Eyupspor fewer than 10.2, since Eyupspor have scored three all season, so the total ends up near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Paul Onuachu, Salah and Muci should test the keeper often against the league's weakest defence, but Eyupspor's own contribution will be small, so I stay close to ten.
